consumersModel.breakageAssessment: If iSeries_Model__c becomes canonical (value diverted out of Model_Number__c), the breakage is concentrated and asymmetric: it only affects Hardware_Platform__c = iSeries records (today exactly the 46 rows the bug already created, and all future iSeries records). The reporter's hypothesis that 'iSeries_Model__c is the correct field to keep' is WRONG as a blanket statement, because multiple production readers consult Model_Number__c and NONE of them fall back to iSeries_Model__c. Concrete silent breaks: (1) BSSOrderInfoRestService emits model=blank for iSeries hardware in the outbound BSS/billing integration payload (genuine downstream system break, not just UI). (2) PowerOrderSplittingService loses the model entirely on cloned iSeries hardware during Power-line splits (iSeries_Model__c not in the clone path). (3) All search/filter paths -- HardwareGroupController model filter (line 103) and HardwareManagementController free-text search (324-325) -- fail to find iSeries hardware by model. (4) Every display surface (hardwareGroupManager datatable+cards, hardwareManagementModal, HardwareProductSelector context, HardwareGroupController group cards) shows blank model for iSeries. Notably SAFE: pricing (HardwareAttributePricingPrehook uses P_Group/Server_Type/Users only -- model is audit-JSON only) and product eligibility (HardwareProductEligibilityService uses processors + feature codes only). The two trigger handlers and the entire License-Key/LKG stack are not consumers at all (different field LPAR_Model_Number__c on License_Key__c). Root architectural finding: Model_Number__c is a free-text length-100 field holding the full model name (e.g. 'IBM Power E1080'), while iSeries_Model__c is a constrained picklist of iSeries short codes (150/170/500/22A/M9S...) and is the CONTROLLING field for the iSeries_Feature_Code__c dependent picklist. They are semantically DISTINCT (FortraDemoDataFactory populates both with different values). The picklist combobox in the LWC is mislabeled 'Model Number' but bound to iSeriesModel; the real-data problem is that the iSeries-model picklist value is the only model captured, while every consumer reads the general Model_Number__c text field.
consumersModel.verdict: DO NOT make iSeries_Model__c the canonical/only field, and do NOT simply blank-promote it over Model_Number__c. Model_Number__c is the field actually consumed by production logic (outbound BSS integration, Power-split clone copy, both search filters, all display surfaces); iSeries_Model__c has NO downstream consumers beyond the LWC's own create flow, its dependent-picklist control of iSeries_Feature_Code__c, and a list view. The two fields are semantically different (free-text full model name vs constrained iSeries short-code picklist), so they are not drop-in substitutes. Recommended fix direction: in the 'Create New Hardware Group' modal, the picklist value chosen must ALSO populate Model_Number__c (the canonical, integration-facing field), not only iSeries_Model__c. Either (a) write the chosen value to BOTH fields (keep iSeries_Model__c for the dependent Feature Code picklist AND set Model_Number__c so BSS/search/display work), or (b) re-point the modal's write to Model_Number__c and drive the dependent picklist differently. Whatever the choice, a backfill is required for the 46 already-diverted records (copy iSeries_Model__c -> Model_Number__c) or they will continue to break the BSS payload and search. Pricing and eligibility need no changes. Treat the LkgRecordCreator/LicenseKeyEmailHandler/QLI-handler/Opp-handler hits as out of scope (false positives)."

Conclusion: the reporter's instinct to KEEP iSeries_Model__c is correct, but the stated root cause ('UI mapped to the wrong DB field / value not saving') is not what's happening. The modal already saves correctly to Hardware__c.iSeries_Model__c — verified in UAT on the screenshot record HW-0717956 (iSeries_Model__c=500). The 46 existing records need NO migration — the display fix surfaces them.

Blast radius: pricing and eligibility are SAFE (no model-based logic). BSS integration is NOT impacted today — only 2 OrderItems reach the 46 records via the BSS lookup and both are on Draft orders. Out of scope / follow-ups to confirm with owners: BSS must-carry-model on activation, search-by-code parity (cls:103, 324-325), PowerOrderSplittingService clone copy (cls:410/424), and a small data cleanup of 3 dual-populated + 2 off-picklist legacy rows.
